speaker: ORB
text: Helmets off.

speaker: ORB
text: These two used to be a band. Four years. One bus. One stage. Two hundred shows and one song anybody remembers.

speaker: ORB
text: She went solo. He's still angry about it. They have not been in the same room since.

speaker: ORB
text: If they survive thirty days on this planet — together — they go home with what's in that crate. If they don't, the crate goes home with me.

speaker: ORB
text: When did the band end?

speaker: PIP
text: Three years ago.

speaker: GRUFF
text: She quit. Mid-tour. Between the soundcheck and the show.

speaker: ORB
text: Still sore.

speaker: ORB
text: Nobody's making you. You can put the helmets back on and I'll fly you home and we never speak of this. But the second those anklets lock, the thirty days are running, and the tether between you does not come off for any reason I can think of.

speaker: GRUFF
text: Running.

speaker: ORB
text: Both locked.

speaker: ORB
text: One rule. This ring is the only door off this planet. Cross this line and you quit. If either of you quits, I take you both home tonight — and the crate goes home with me. There is no version where one of you crosses and the other one stays.

speaker: ORB
text: Have fun down there.

speaker: ORB
text: One thousand metres across. Its own sky, if you squint. Its own sunrise every eleven hours, because I got the spin slightly wrong and I'm not fixing it now. Her camp is at the north pole.

speaker: PIP
text: It's actually kind of nice? The horizon's right there. You could walk to the edge of the world before breakfast.

speaker: ORB
text: His cave is at the south. On a planet this size they can go a week without seeing each other. Which, from what I can tell, is the plan.

speaker: GRUFF
text: It's a hole. I like a hole. Nobody sings in a hole.

speaker: ORB
text: He's brought one mattress, one paperback, and a rock he uses as a second rock. That's the whole inventory. She brought a keyboard. Neither of them has mentioned the other's luggage.

speaker: ORB
text: That's THE COUNT. It keeps the day and it keeps the size. The size is the only thing on this planet that changes — and it only ever goes one way.

speaker: ORB
text: Facilities.

speaker: ORB
text: And on the equator: the crate. Sealed. Nobody opens it before Day 20. Not them. Not me. It has a lock and I do not have hands.

speaker: PIP
text: You don't know what's in it?

speaker: ORB
text: I know exactly what's in it. That's the whole point of me.

speaker: PIP
text: Sooner or later one of us has to bring it up. I'm hoping it's later. I'm hoping it's Day 29 and we're both too tired to do it properly.

speaker: GRUFF
text: I've been cold to her. I'm allowed. She left. You don't get a warm welcome for leaving; you get a cave.

speaker: ORB
text: They think this is about surviving. It isn't. Nobody has ever failed to survive one of my planets. What they fail is each other.

speaker: ORB
text: Day two. Here's the engine. Every deal I offer them shrinks this planet. Not a fine, not a penalty, not a score. Rock, gone, forever. They can say no to any deal. Most people don't, because the deals are very good and the rock is very boring.

speaker: ORB
text: Right now they can avoid each other. At three hundred metres they'll share a sunrise whether they like it or not. At a hundred metres they'll hear each other breathe. At two, there's nowhere to stand but together.

speaker: ORB
text: So. Does a smaller world bring them back — or finish them off? I genuinely don't know. That's why I built it.

speaker: GRUFF
text: Two metres. He said two metres.

speaker: PIP
text: I heard him.

speaker: ORB
text: For the record, nobody has ever reached two metres on one of my planets. The furthest anyone got was nineteen, and they crossed the ring on Day 22 holding hands, which I still think about.

speaker: ORB
text: Day four. You've spoken eleven words to each other. I counted. Eight of them were "the tether's caught again." So — first offer.

speaker: ORB
text: Under the left lid: nothing changes. You keep your thousand-metre planet, your two poles, your week of silence.

speaker: ORB
text: Under the right lid: I halve it. Five hundred metres, starting at tomorrow's sunrise. And I add a hundred thousand to whatever is in the crate. You don't know what's in the crate, so you don't know what a hundred thousand is on top of. That's the fun part.

speaker: GRUFF
text: Money's money.

speaker: PIP
text: We haven't seen each other in three days. We could live at five hundred. It's still a whole planet.

speaker: GRUFF
text: We could live at fifty. I lived in a van with you.

speaker: PIP
text: You lived in the van's back seat. I lived up front. That's why the band lasted four years.

speaker: ORB
text: I need a lid.

speaker: PIP
text: Halve it.

speaker: ORB
text: Their first camp was on that piece. Her first tent. His first dent in the wall. It's on its way somewhere else now.

speaker: GRUFF
text: Huh.

speaker: PIP
text: That was — that was a lot of planet.

speaker: ORB
text: Half. It was half. I did say.

speaker: GRUFF
text: Doesn't come back?

speaker: ORB
text: Nothing on this show comes back. That's the show.

speaker: PIP
text: I picked that.

speaker: GRUFF
text: You picked it. I'd have picked it. Doesn't matter who says the word when both of you are looking at the same lid.

speaker: ORB
text: Less than a day at half size, and it's already going wrong. Half the rock means half the gravity has somewhere else to be. Both camps are now sliding into the same valley, one peg at a time, and neither of them has noticed yet.

speaker: ORB
text: His snoring carries. All the way round. It arrives at her tent from both directions at once, which is a thing that only happens on a planet this size, and I did not plan it, and I love it.

speaker: PIP
text: He did this on the bus. Every night for four years. I forgot. How did I forget.

speaker: PIP
text: Nope. Nope nope nope.

speaker: ORB
text: Day six. She was going to wake him. She was going to say something. She counted to three and left. I have the whole thing on eleven cameras.

speaker: GRUFF
text: I wasn't asleep.

speaker: ORB
text: He wasn't asleep. He waited until she'd gone and then he snored for another hour, on purpose, in her direction.

speaker: PIP
text: Tether me to anyone else. Anyone. Pick a name off the street. Whoever it is would at least ask me mine.

speaker: PIP
text: Six days. You've said nine words to me. I counted. He counted. There are cameras that counted.

speaker: GRUFF
text: You'd rather be anywhere I'm not. That's the whole story. It's always been the whole story. You had a whole planet and you camped at the far end of it.

speaker: PIP
text: Because you took the cave!

speaker: GRUFF
text: Because you took the band!

speaker: PIP
text: You wrote one song in four years! One! And it was about your van!

speaker: GRUFF
text: It was a good van.

speaker: PIP
text: It was a good van! It was the only thing on that tour you ever loved out loud!

speaker: ORB
text: Nobody wins this one. I want to be clear about that, because there's a version of this show where I'd cut in and offer them something, and this is not that version. Some things you have to let run out.

speaker: PIP
text: Clean slate?

speaker: GRUFF
text: …Fine.

speaker: PIP
text: That's a yes?

speaker: GRUFF
text: It's a fine. Fine is what I've got.

speaker: GRUFF
text: I don't know how to do a clean slate. Drummers don't get one. You hit the thing, the thing makes the noise, the noise is already gone. There's no going back and hitting it softer.

speaker: ORB
text: Twenty-four more days. Four hundred and ninety-eight metres of rock left to lose. And that's the first time either of them has said "fine" and meant it.

speaker: ORB
text: Day ten. That one was on the house. No deal, no money, no choice, no lid. I took two hundred metres because I felt like it and because you've been boring.

speaker: GRUFF
text: You can just do that?

speaker: ORB
text: I can just do that. It's my rock. You're renting.

speaker: ORB
text: Gift: THE COUNT gets thrusters. It can fetch things now. Ration bars, the tether when it's caught, small rocks you want thrown at each other. Try not to break it; it's the only one that likes you both.

speaker: ORB
text: And from here on, the money gets serious. So will the planet. There's a crate on the equator and ten days until it opens and I'd think about what a hundred thousand looks like when it's sitting on top of something.

speaker: PIP
text: Who did that?

speaker: GRUFF
text: Rocks fall. They land how they land.

speaker: PIP
text: In a heart.

speaker: GRUFF
text: It's a bad heart. It's more of a — a kidney.

speaker: PIP
text: It's a good kidney.

speaker: ORB
text: He didn't mention it. She noticed he kept it. He's been stepping around it for two days so his feet don't ruin the shape.

speaker: ORB
text: Day twelve. Three hundred metres means one sunrise for both of them now. They've stopped pretending the vent is only warm on one side. So I asked the question I've been saving.

speaker: ORB
text: So what actually broke the band?

speaker: PIP
text: I sat in the dressing room every night thinking nobody in that band would notice if I vanished. So I vanished first. Before anyone could not notice.

speaker: GRUFF
text: I noticed.

speaker: GRUFF
text: I just never said it out loud. I thought if I said it you'd know I was watching the door.

speaker: PIP
text: You were watching the door?

speaker: GRUFF
text: Every night. Four years. I know what the back of your head looks like leaving better than I know your face.

speaker: PIP
text: That's the worst thing anyone's ever said to me.

speaker: GRUFF
text: It's the nicest thing I've got.

speaker: PIP
text: I thought you were the one who didn't care. You never said anything. The others said things. Wrong things, but things.

speaker: GRUFF
text: I hit a drum for a living. Saying things was your job.

speaker: PIP
text: So what happens to us now?

speaker: GRUFF
text: Sit here. It's warm. That's a plan.

speaker: PIP
text: That's not a plan, that's a chair.

speaker: GRUFF
text: Then it's a chair. I've had worse plans.

speaker: ORB
text: That's the moment the show stopped being about the crate. I'll keep pretending otherwise for the money, but you should know.

speaker: GRUFF
text: I haven't seen further than thirty metres in two weeks. Everywhere I look, the ground gets in the way of the ground.

speaker: ORB
text: Forty seconds. Pole to pole and back. He tried to walk it off and it walked him back.

speaker: GRUFF
text: I'm not doing great. In the head.

speaker: GRUFF
text: On the bus you could at least look out the window and see something that wasn't the bus.

speaker: PIP
text: He used to say that about the bus too.

speaker: ORB
text: Fourteen days in. Three hundred metres. Here's what I've learned: it isn't the size that gets them. It's the lap. The moment you can walk all the way round your life in under a minute and end up looking at your own footprints. Everyone I've put down here hits it around the two-week mark, and the ones who make it are the ones who sit down next to somebody when they do.

speaker: ORB
text: Day fifteen. Halfway. I've been listening. He wants to see further than thirty metres. So: a dome. Real air. Real trees. Real shade, real birds, a horizon you can't reach in forty seconds. All of it is yours — if the planet goes to a hundred metres.

speaker: GRUFF
text: Trees.

speaker: PIP
text: A hundred metres. Fifteen days at a hundred metres, and then whatever comes after a hundred.

speaker: PIP
text: …No.

speaker: ORB
text: Ten seconds to change your mind.

speaker: GRUFF
text: There were trees.

speaker: PIP
text: There were trees on a hundred-metre rock with fifteen days left. I did the maths on your face.

speaker: ORB
text: Regret it yet?

speaker: GRUFF
text: I'll let you know at ninety metres.

speaker: ORB
text: Remember — there's still a crate. Five days. And nobody's said no to it yet.

speaker: ORB
text: She's not sure. Neither am I. It was a very good dome.

speaker: GRUFF
text: I'd have kept the trees for the whole fifteen days. I'd have named them. That's all I'm saying.

speaker: ORB
text: Day sixteen. Breakfast. She's arranged it. He's going to pretend he hasn't noticed the shape, and then he's going to eat it from the outside in so the shape lasts.

speaker: PIP
text: Bandmates?

speaker: GRUFF
text: Bandmates.

speaker: PIP
text: That's the first thing you've agreed to in sixteen days.

speaker: GRUFF
text: I agreed to "fine."

speaker: PIP
text: Fine isn't agreeing. Fine is surrendering slowly.

speaker: ORB
text: He's on chapter three. Chapter three is "Hitting Things Is Not A Conversation." He has underlined it. He has underlined it hard enough to go through to chapter four.

speaker: PIP
text: He's taking notes. On a rock. With his hand.

speaker: ORB
text: Chapter four is "Say The Thing Before The Rock Runs Out." I didn't write the book. I did leave it in the cave.

speaker: PIP
text: You still wear that thing? It's been cracked since the second tour.

speaker: GRUFF
text: It's been cracked since the last night of the second tour. Specific night.

speaker: PIP
text: Why keep a broken one?

speaker: GRUFF
text: There's something about it I'll tell you.

speaker: GRUFF
text: The last night on this rock. Not before. If I tell you before, you'll be nice to me for the wrong reasons for two weeks and I'd rather have the right ones for one day.

speaker: ORB
text: Fourteen days. He's just told her the only way to hear the end of that sentence is to stay for it. I could not have written it better, and I did try.

speaker: ORB
text: Day nineteen. The crate opens tomorrow, and tonight you choose how. Five platters. Every one of them opens the crate; every one of them costs something. You pick one, the crate opens at sunrise, the price is paid at sunrise. Careful — one of these lids is a trap and one of them is a gift, and they look the same from up here.

speaker: ORB
text: Pay two hundred thousand out of whatever's in the crate.

speaker: GRUFF
text: No. We don't know what's in it. Could be two hundred thousand.

speaker: ORB
text: Five hundred thousand.

speaker: GRUFF
text: No. Same reason, bigger.

speaker: ORB
text: Shrink the planet. Three hundred metres to twenty-five. A house. One house, in space, for the last ten days.

speaker: PIP
text: Twenty-five. We'd be in the same room. Every room.

speaker: GRUFF
text: Take it.

speaker: PIP
text: Take it.

speaker: ORB
text: You're sure. There are two lids left.

speaker: GRUFF
text: Rock's rock. We've got plenty. Take it.

speaker: ORB
text: Lid three. That's the one. At sunrise the crate opens and the planet pays.

speaker: ORB
text: Free. Platter four was free. Open the crate, pay nothing, keep three hundred metres of planet.

speaker: GRUFF
text: It was free.

speaker: ORB
text: It was free. You took the house.

speaker: PIP
text: You said one of them was a gift.

speaker: ORB
text: I did. I say it every time. Nobody has ever lifted lid four first. I don't know why. I've stopped hoping.

speaker: GRUFF
text: We had plenty of rock.

speaker: ORB
text: You had plenty of rock. At sunrise you'll have a house. Sleep on it. It's already done.

speaker: ORB
text: Day twenty. The bill comes at sunrise. Twenty-five metres. Tents, crate, pad, toilet, the vent, the two of them. On a house.

speaker: ORB
text: Two tickets on the rescue ship. Not money. Passage. You both go home. Whoever wins, whoever doesn't, whatever happens in the next ten days — both of you leave this rock on the same ship.

speaker: GRUFF
text: That's the redemption. Right there. That's the whole thing, in a box.

speaker: PIP
text: We both go home.

speaker: GRUFF
text: We both go home.

speaker: ORB
text: For twenty days that crate has been the reason to stay. Now it's the reason there's nothing left to fight about — which, I promise you, is the most dangerous thing I can give two people who've just started being kind to each other.

speaker: ORB
text: The tickets aren't free. Look down.

speaker: ORB
text: Twenty-five metres. They cannot be out of arm's reach. Sleeping, washing, the toilet — everything within three metres of the other one, for ten days, with a tether that has never once been the right length.

speaker: GRUFF
text: You're humming it again.

speaker: PIP
text: I'm not humming anything.

speaker: GRUFF
text: Four notes. Breakfast. You've done it nine times.

speaker: PIP
text: Ten. You missed one in the toilet.

speaker: GRUFF
text: I heard that one. I was being polite.

speaker: PIP
text: There's no rock left to lose.

speaker: ORB
text: There's twenty-three metres of it.

speaker: ORB
text: Day twenty-five. New rules. Everything up to now was shared. Shared planet, shared crate, shared ship. That's over.

speaker: ORB
text: The escape pod launch key. The pod has one seat. Whoever turns this key goes home now — with the whole prize: both tickets, and the whole hundred thousand I put on the crate on Day 4. The other one gets nothing. No ticket. No fifty. They wait here for the ship on Day 30 with an empty crate and a lot of time to think.

speaker: GRUFF
text: And if nobody turns it?

speaker: ORB
text: Then Day 30 comes, the hundred splits down the middle, and you both go home like the crate promised. The key is only for the one who can't wait.

speaker: ORB
text: And from today the planet loses size every single day. Twenty. Twelve. Seven. Four. Two. You'll be able to reach the key from anywhere on the planet by Wednesday.

speaker: PIP
text: He's looking at it.

speaker: ORB
text: He's looking at it.

speaker: ORB
text: Five days. Five sizes. One key. And the only thing I've ever seen make somebody turn a key like that is a good reason — which, thanks to Day 12, they've both got.

speaker: ORB
text: This is the part I like. Green for truth. Red for a lie. Stand in it, ask each other anything, and the beam tells the other one whether to believe you. Nobody has ever enjoyed this part except me.

speaker: GRUFF
text: Anything?

speaker: ORB
text: Anything. The beam doesn't judge the question. Only the answer.

speaker: GRUFF
text: Were you better off solo?

speaker: PIP
text: No.

speaker: GRUFF
text: Huh.

speaker: PIP
text: I had a bigger room and a smaller everything else. I sang to people who'd never heard the van song. It was fine. Fine is surrendering slowly. You taught me that this week.

speaker: ORB
text: Verified. Filed. She won't be able to take that back on Day 30, and she knows it.

speaker: GRUFF
text: Bigger room. Smaller everything else. You should've written that one down.

speaker: PIP
text: I did. It's the second verse.

speaker: PIP
text: Would you launch the pod?

speaker: GRUFF
text: I'd never leave you on a rock.

speaker: ORB
text: Unverified. Technical fault. THE COUNT ran into the projector. Moving on.

speaker: PIP
text: Can he say it again?

speaker: ORB
text: He can say anything he likes. The beam's done for today.

speaker: GRUFF
text: Same question. To you.

speaker: PIP
text: No.

speaker: ORB
text: Two answers to the same question. Hers is green. His is a shrug from a broken machine. That gap is going to sit between them for five days and I am not going to fix the machine.

speaker: GRUFF
text: The goggle's got nothing to do with it.

speaker: PIP
text: I didn't say the goggle.

speaker: GRUFF
text: You looked at it.

speaker: PIP
text: I look at it every day. It's on your face.

speaker: GRUFF
text: She got her happy ending on camera. Green light, big room, "no, I wasn't better off." Everyone saw it. She's fine now. She's done.

speaker: GRUFF
text: I could take the whole prize and be gone before she wakes up. Nobody would even blame me. She left first. The whole planet's been telling her she left first.

speaker: GRUFF
text: I'm just saying I could. I'm not saying anything else. Put that on the beam.

speaker: ORB
text: He said that to a camera he thinks is off. It isn't. Nothing here is off. But I'm not showing her this, because the beam wouldn't have, and I like to be consistent.

speaker: ORB
text: Day twenty-six. Twelve metres. A bus. They have, I'm told, done a bus. So today they each get a soundproof pod and a question, and neither hears the other's answer. I do.

speaker: PIP
text: Maybe he wants it to be even. Maybe after what I did, that's fair. I left him on a stage. He leaves me on a rock. That's — that's a kind of song.

speaker: ORB
text: You're not planning to launch alone, are you?

speaker: GRUFF
text: …Is that a rule or a question?

speaker: ORB
text: It was a yes-or-no question.

speaker: GRUFF
text: Then put me down as a maybe. Write that down.

speaker: ORB
text: I wrote it down. I write everything down. She doesn't know he said maybe, and he doesn't know she thinks he'd be right to. Twelve metres and the biggest gap on the planet is the one between those two pods.

speaker: PIP
text: Put me down.

speaker: GRUFF
text: Where?

speaker: PIP
text: Anywhere that's the ground!

speaker: GRUFF
text: It's all the ground. It's seven metres of the ground. Pick a metre.

speaker: PIP
text: I'm picking the one you're not standing on.

speaker: GRUFF
text: That's a small metre.

speaker: ORB
text: Day twenty-seven. She's stopped pretending she isn't humming it. He's stopped pretending he doesn't know what it is.

speaker: ORB
text: Day twenty-eight. Four metres. He is taller than the planet. I've been waiting twenty-eight days to say that sentence.

speaker: GRUFF
text: Every bump makes me want to hit that lever. Every time the tether catches. Every time she breathes on my elbow, because there's nowhere on this rock she isn't breathing on my elbow.

speaker: PIP
text: The beam never said yes for you.

speaker: GRUFF
text: The beam broke.

speaker: PIP
text: The beam broke on you. It didn't break on me.

speaker: GRUFF
text: Ask me about the goggle instead.

speaker: PIP
text: Tomorrow. You said.

speaker: GRUFF
text: Tomorrow. Two metres. If there's a tomorrow that's got two metres in it.

speaker: PIP
text: I think he's getting ready to leave.

speaker: ORB
text: Two metres. Twenty-four hours. The last night on this rock. He said "not before." It's not before.

speaker: GRUFF
text: I sold the tour van.

speaker: PIP
text: You loved that van. You wrote a song about that van.

speaker: GRUFF
text: I was buying you a solo ticket. Real one. Real label. Your name on it. I had it in an envelope. I was going to give it to you on stage, last night of the tour, in front of everybody, so you'd know the band was giving it to you and not taking it from you.

speaker: GRUFF
text: You left the week before. The goggle cracked the night I found out. I don't remember how. I remember the floor.

speaker: PIP
text: That's why you kept it.

speaker: GRUFF
text: That's why I kept it. Cracked's the right shape for it.

speaker: PIP
text: You could have said. Any night. Any of the four years.

speaker: GRUFF
text: I'm saying it now. Two metres. It's the only rock small enough to make me.

speaker: ORB
text: For the record: that's the first time in thirty days he's said a whole paragraph. The book gets some credit. The rock gets most of it.

speaker: ORB
text: And now she has to decide whether a man who sold his van for her would also leave her on a rock for a crate. The beam didn't tell her. I'm not going to either.

speaker: PIP
text: I'm scared of the next twenty-four hours.

speaker: PIP
text: Not the rock. Not the ship. Him. I'm scared of what he does while I'm asleep, when the only thing I can do is keep being asleep.

speaker: GRUFF
text: The whole prize would change my life more than half of it. That's just true. Fifty is a new van. A hundred is a room with a drum kit in it and a door that shuts.

speaker: GRUFF
text: And after this we might never talk again anyway. We didn't for three years. We were fine. She was fine. Fine is surrendering slowly.

speaker: ORB
text: Eleven hours and seven minutes. The key is eighty centimetres from his hand. It's been eighty centimetres from his hand for four days.

speaker: ORB
text: For those keeping score: she's been verified twice. He's been verified never. She's asleep. He's not. And the rock is exactly the size of the decision.

speaker: ORB
text: Eight minutes. Eight minutes, and then the ship, and then the split, and then none of this matters. Unless somebody turns a key.

speaker: PIP
text: Don't. Whatever you're doing, don't do it yet. Tell me about the van again. Tell me anything.

speaker: GRUFF
text: I'm not doing anything. I'm standing here. It's a very small rock.

speaker: ORB
text: Fifty-eight seconds. Last call for the pod. After this it locks and the key is a souvenir.

speaker: GRUFF
text: Fifty is a van.

speaker: PIP
text: Fifty is a van and a drummer. A hundred is a room and nobody in it.

speaker: ORB
text: Nine seconds.

speaker: ORB
text: Three.

speaker: ORB
text: Two.

speaker: ORB
text: One.

speaker: ORB
text: Time's up.

speaker: GRUFF
text: I said I'd never leave you on a rock.

speaker: PIP
text: The beam didn't say.

speaker: GRUFF
text: The beam was never going to. That's what I liked about it.

speaker: PIP
text: Your hand was on that lever a long time.

speaker: GRUFF
text: Forty-nine seconds. I was counting. Drummer.

speaker: ORB
text: Fifty thousand each — that's the hundred I put on the crate on Day 4, split down the middle — and both tickets. Somebody said "halve it" that night, and I keep my word even when nobody remembers I gave it.

speaker: ORB
text: So — where does the band go from here?

speaker: ORB
text: I asked a question and got a drum solo. Four notes. I've had worse answers from the beam.

speaker: GRUFF
text: Band's got a planet now. Small one.

speaker: PIP
text: Two metres. We've done smaller. We did a van.

speaker: ORB
text: Band's back. Subscribe.
